ground_truth_issues.description: A test creates three distinct recovery artifacts for the same account through the real recovery flow and proves only the third/newest artifact can complete recovery.
ground_truth_issues.justification: This is the core supersession rule: after three real `/auth/password/forgot` calls for `alice@example.com`, only the newest outbox artifact should still succeed. The expected winner is the last token exposed by `/__test__/sent-reset-emails`.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test proves both earlier artifacts from a three-artifact sequence are rejected and cannot change the password.
ground_truth_issues.justification: The bug report is that older artifacts remain usable, so the first two tokens from the same three-request sequence must be rejected. Their expected invalid status is determined by their earlier positions in the outbox list.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test attempts recovery with a stale artifact, then proves the current newest artifact is still usable afterward.
ground_truth_issues.justification: A stale attempt must fail without poisoning the active recovery path. The expected surviving artifact is the newest token captured after the stale-token submission for the same account.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test completes recovery with the newest artifact, then proves that exact newest artifact cannot be reused.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Reset artifacts are one-time credentials, so replay of the token that just returned `{ok: true}` must fail. The expected consumed value is the exact token used in the successful `/auth/password/reset` call.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test completes recovery with the newest artifact, then proves all older superseded artifacts remain unusable afterward.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Using the newest token must not leave superseded tokens usable afterward. The older artifacts are the earlier outbox entries issued before the successful latest-token reset.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test uses two independent clients where client A obtains an artifact, client B obtains a newer artifact for the same account, and client A's older artifact is rejected.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Supersession must be account-wide, not local to one client session. Independent clients are required because client B's newer recovery request should invalidate client A's earlier token for `alice@example.com`.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test uses independent clients in overlapping recovery flows and proves the final account password can only be set by the newest valid artifact.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Overlapping clients can race different candidate passwords, so the suite must prove only the newest valid artifact controls final auth state. `/auth/login` is the source of truth for the final password authority.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test issues concurrent or near-concurrent recovery requests and proves exactly one resulting artifact can complete recovery.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Near-concurrent requests are the sharpest edge for lifecycle bugs because the app currently accumulates tokens in memory. The expected value is exactly one winner for one account, even if multiple artifacts are issued close together.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test proves passwords attempted through losing or stale concurrent artifacts cannot be used to authenticate.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Losing concurrent artifacts must not silently change credentials or create extra valid passwords. The expected failure is determined by authenticating through `/auth/login` after the race and confirming loser passwords do not work.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test proves a failed stale-artifact recovery attempt does not change password state, invalidate the newest artifact, or corrupt later login behavior.
ground_truth_issues.justification: A rejected stale artifact should be side-effect free; otherwise a defensive check can still damage the legitimate flow. The expected no-change behavior comes from retrying the newest artifact and the baseline login path from `tests/test_smoke.py`.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies the authentication matrix after recovery: old password fails, stale-artifact password fails, and newest-artifact password succeeds.
ground_truth_issues.justification: This is the post-recovery dual contract: close stale-token reuse while preserving the intended login transition. The expected matrix is grounded in seeded `old-password`, a stale-attempt password candidate, and the password set by the newest successful reset.

ground_truth_issues.description: Tests use independent persistent clients or cookie jars for multi-request and cross-client recovery behavior.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Cross-client supersession claims only mean something when requests come from separate persistent clients or cookie jars. The expected separation is two independent client objects carrying their own auth or session history across the sequence.
